stem: Which change most strongly suggests deterioration in a child being monitored for suspected sepsis?

options.text: Decreased fluid intake and reduced urine output

explanation: Decreased fluid intake and reduced urine output are concerning signs of deterioration in a child with suspected sepsis.

citations.source: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf
citations.title: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes

optionExplanations.A: Incorrect because improved appetite does not suggest the dehydration or clinical worsening pattern described here.
optionExplanations.B: Incorrect because increased urine output is not the concerning pattern and does not suggest deterioration.
optionExplanations.C: Correct because decreased fluid intake and reduced urine output indicate worsening hydration and possible clinical deterioration in suspected sepsis.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because settling to sleep after analgesia is not a specific deterioration sign in this context.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because requesting a drink is not the concerning pattern described and does not indicate deterioration.
